description: Stable extension SPI for Skill Family profiles and project adoption declarations. A profile may only DECLARE its finite differences from the common core; a project profile declares its adopting workspace. Enforcement is mechanical with stable result codes.

descriptor.note: The descriptor is the provider intake surface. It is plain validated data (additionalProperties: false at every level), so a profile cannot smuggle behavior in through the descriptor itself. SPI v3 also defines the separate project-profile intake; provider validation composes the optional top-level sections `adoption` and `overrides` onto the contracts profile-descriptor schema before validating; the contracts package stays untouched.

projectProfile.note: The project profile is the scaffolded workspace adoption declaration and is never accepted by verifyProfile.

principles: declaration-only: differences are data declarations interpreted by the core's own fixed logic; a profile never supplies behavior that the core executes as core logic
closed-core: no difference may add, override, or remove anything owned by the common core (contracts objects, registered protocols, kernel operations, core packages, kit commands)
open-extension-points: overrides and removals may only target extension points this SPI explicitly opens; everything else is closed by default
contained-write-set: every path-like declaration must resolve strictly inside the profile's own directory (the descriptor's directory); a profile writes nothing outside itself

data-only-resources: SPI entrypoints are JSON data resources, never executable modules; they are read through the containment layer, parsed deterministically, and must be one plain data object with a fixed key set; verification never imports, evaluates, or executes anything a profile provides
frozen-base: a profile extends exactly the loaded frozen contracts base version

verified-adoption: an adoption declaration is optional, but when present it is complete or refused: the minimal field set is mandatory, the pin covers exactly the three Foundation packages, and every declared digest is compared against the real artifact bytes inside the write set

tightening-only-overrides: an override reuses an existing rule id with a project-level numeric value and must strictly tighten the frozen catalog baseline in the parameter's declared direction; relaxation and equality are refused

resultCodes.name: OK
resultCodes.meaning: The provider descriptor or project profile and all applicable declarations satisfy every SPI rule; the input is admitted as a declaration-only extension or project adoption declaration.

resultCodes.name: DESCRIPTOR_INVALID
resultCodes.meaning: The descriptor failed the SPI-composed extended profile-descriptor schema under the declared dialect and strict policy, or could not be parsed as JSON. Adoption field completeness and pin format are schema-checked here. The observed contracts code (for example SFC1001) is carried in details.observedCode.

resultCodes.name: MISSING_RESOURCE
resultCodes.meaning: A declared resource does not exist or does not satisfy its own declaration: an entrypoint file is absent, cannot be read inside the write set, is not parseable as a JSON data resource, omits required declaration keys, or its declared id/version contradicts the descriptor entry.

resultCodes.name: WRITE_SET_ESCAPE
resultCodes.meaning: A path-like declaration (SPI entrypoint or path-like difference target) does not resolve strictly inside the profile's own directory, or is an ambiguous/absolute/cross-platform path. The profile write set is its own directory and nothing else.

resultCodes.name: CORE_REVERSE_DEPENDENCY
resultCodes.meaning: The profile attempts to make the core depend on it: a difference targets a core-owned name, an override/removal targets a surface the SPI does not open, an entrypoint is declared as an executable module (behavior injection, refused before any of its bytes are interpreted), or a parsed declaration contains non-data values.

resultCodes.name: BASE_MISMATCH
resultCodes.meaning: The descriptor declares a base contracts version different from the loaded frozen contracts base; differences must be declared against the frozen base only.

resultCodes.name: ADOPTION_PIN_UNVERIFIED
resultCodes.meaning: The descriptor declares an adoption section, but the pin cannot be verified against real files (GK-4 real-file digest discipline): a pinned artifact path is absent or unreadable inside the profile write set, or its actual sha256 differs from the declared digest. details carries the failing package, path, declared and actual digests.

resultCodes.name: OVERRIDE_POLICY_VIOLATION
resultCodes.meaning: An overrides entry violates the tightening-only policy: the rule id does not exist in the frozen rule baseline catalog, the parameter is not registered for that rule, the same rule/parameter pair is declared twice, or the numeric value does not strictly tighten the catalog baseline in the parameter's declared direction (relaxation and equality are both refused).

resultCodes.name: PROJECT_PROFILE_INVALID
resultCodes.meaning: The project-level profile cannot be read, parsed, or validated against the project-profile contract. Pin and override failures retain SPE1006 and SPE1007.

extensionPoints.description: Declares how profile artifacts are projected across fictional hosts. Data-only projection plan; the core owns the projection mechanism.
Declares render facts for profile owned artifacts (pages, documents). Data-only render declaration; the core owns rendering execution.
Declares a public-surface scan policy for profile outputs. Data-only policy declaration; the core owns scan execution.

coreOwned.note: Static part of the core-owned target set. The loader derives the dynamic part (contracts objects, registered schema $ids, protocol names, kernel operation names) from the contracts package at runtime, so those cannot drift. An independent audit cross-checks the static lists below against the real packages.

writeSet.root: the directory containing the descriptor file (the profile's own directory)
writeSet.rule: every path-like declaration must lexically and canonically resolve strictly inside the write-set root; absolute, UNC, drive, traversal, and symlink-escaping paths are rejected

declarationShape.jsonRoundTrip: the exported value must survive JSON.parse(JSON.stringify(value)) unchanged
declarationShape.consistency: exported id and spiVersion must equal the descriptor's spi entry id and version; exported extensionPoint must be one of this SPI's open extension points

entrypointRules.note: Data-only Profile SPI: SPI entrypoints are JSON data resources. Verification never imports, evaluates, or executes any profile-provided file. An entrypoint whose file name carries an executable module extension is behavior injection and is refused as SPE1004 before any of its bytes are read or interpreted; remaining entrypoints are read through the containment layer and parsed as JSON only.
entrypointRules.parsing: JSON.parse only; callables, symbols, bigints, getters, and proxies cannot survive JSON parsing; the declaration-shape checks remain as defense in depth

adoptionDeclaration.note: Minimal adoption field set per remediation handoff D-8 (adoption-lock concept deprecated): the adoption proof is this declaration, machine-verified by verifyProfile. The type definitions live in profiles/spi/profile-adoption.schema.json ($defs.adoption). Every consumer that renders or scaffolds a profile.json template (engineering-kit scaffold skeleton included) must reuse exactly this minimal set; on conflict this definition wins.

packageFields.version: exact semver version of the pinned package
packageFields.path: relative POSIX path of the pinned artifact inside the profile write set
packageFields.sha256: 64-char lowercase hex digest of the artifact bytes

foundation_pin.digestDiscipline: GK-4 migrated: every digest declared in a profile is compared against the real file bytes by verifyProfile (adoption-pin-digests step, verifyAdoptionDigests export); a missing artifact or a mismatched digest is SPE1006

overridesPolicy.note: Self-tightening declarations per remediation handoff D-6: no new rule ids are minted; an override reuses the original rule id plus a project-level numeric value. Type definitions live in profiles/spi/profile-adoption.schema.json ($defs.overrides); the verification input is the local rule baseline catalog profiles/spi/rule-baseline-catalog.json (no hard dependency on the audit repository). Risk identification for false tightening (fake tightening, tightening used to mask violations) belongs to skill-failure-auditor, not to this mechanical check.
checks: rule id existence against the frozen catalog (SPE1007 unknown-rule-id)
parameter registered for that rule (SPE1007 unknown-parameter)

numeric value strictly tightens the baseline in the parameter's declared direction: not-increase means strictly less, not-decrease means strictly greater; equality is not tightening (SPE1007 override-not-tightening)
